```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source("R/paper-profile-characterisation.R")
analysis <- build_paper_profiles()
source("R/enroute-level-exposure.R")
enroute <- build_enroute_exposure(analysis)
source("R/paper-lookup-table.R")
lookup <- build_paper_lookup(analysis,enroute)
plots <- plot_paper_profiles(analysis)
fmt <- function(x, digits=0) formatC(x, format="f", digits=digits, big.mark=",")
inv <- function(region, field) analysis$inventory[[field]][analysis$inventory$REGION==region]
med <- function(region, metric) analysis$summary$P50[analysis$summary$REGION==region & analysis$summary$METRIC==metric]
cell <- function(region, metric, scale=1, digits=1) {
  z <- subset(analysis$summary, REGION==region & METRIC==metric)
  paste0(fmt(z$P50*scale,digits), " [",fmt(z$P20*scale,digits), "; ",fmt(z$P80*scale,digits),"]")
}
# Wrapping paragraph columns avoid longtable in two-column PDF output.
paper_table <- function(data, caption, widths=NULL) {
  if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
    if (is.null(widths)) widths <- rep(.94/ncol(data), ncol(data))
    tab <- knitr::kable(data, format="latex", booktabs=TRUE, row.names=FALSE, escape=TRUE)
    spec <- paste0("@{}",paste0("p{",widths,"\\linewidth}",collapse=""),"@{}")
    lines <- strsplit(tab,"\n",fixed=TRUE)[[1]]
    lines[grepl("\\begin{tabular}",lines,fixed=TRUE)] <- paste0("\\begin{tabular}{",spec,"}")
    cat("\\begin{table}[htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{",caption,"}\n\\footnotesize\n\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{2pt}\n\\renewcommand{\\arraystretch}{1.08}\n",paste(lines,collapse="\n"),"\n\\end{table}\n",sep="")
  } else print(knitr::kable(data, caption=caption, row.names=FALSE))
}
```

# Introduction

- Environmental motivation carried forward from @ma2025fuel: quantify aviation fuel consumption and associated emissions, and identify operational opportunities for improvement.
- Performance-monitoring link: translate observed differences in time, distance and vertical profiles into contextual fuel-consumption references.
- Practical need: detailed performance models and operator fuel records have access and computational constraints; compact empirical lookup tables can complement trajectory-based modelling.
- Starting point in the 2025 paper: attach cumulative fuel to characteristic trajectory milestones, reducing full trajectories to comparable phases [@ma2025fuel].
- Extension: the expanded summer-2025 sample supports aircraft/stage-length stratification, regional profile characterisation, and source-aware percentile references.
- Keep two questions distinct: **regional operations** (do comparable aircraft encounter different profiles?) and **conditional consumption** (for comparable aircraft and profiles, are consumption distributions similar?).
- Intended contribution: a compact phase-reference lookup that preserves total fuel alongside rates, with explicit profile definitions and sample support; descriptive references do not establish ATM-recoverable savings.

<!-- Final allocation: approximately 1 page. -->

# Background

- Prior study: milestone discretisation and distance-defined phases; its whole-flight regressions are not phase lookup coefficients or validation targets [@ma2025fuel].
- Comparative design: aircraft type, distance, phase and profile dimensions. Describe regional profile distributions before matching on profile.
- Keep CCO/CDO concepts separate from empirical interruption descriptors and demonstrated fuel effects [@eurocontrol2020ccocdo].

<!-- Final allocation: no more than 2 pages; likely 1-1.5 to accommodate references. -->

# Model, concept, and methods

## Trajectory profile and milestones

The analytical backbone is a trajectory carrying time, pressure altitude, cumulative consumed fuel and cumulative flown distance. The whole-airborne partition is **climb = ATOT--TOC; enroute = TOC--TOD; descent = TOD--ALDT**. Climb and descent therefore include airborne LTO portions. A finer fuel-accounting partition can distinguish climb-out (ATOT--DLTO) and approach/landing (ALTO--ALDT) without changing the whole-airborne interval.

```{r}
#| label: fig-concept
#| fig-cap: "Schematic milestone profile (not study data). Pressure-altitude and airport-distance anchors are additional descriptors, not alternative TOC/TOD definitions."
#| fig-width: 3.45
#| fig-height: 1.85
z <- data.frame(t=c(0,4,10,15,21,45,52,59,70,76),h=c(0,0,10,17,34,34,31,31,8,0))
ggplot(z,aes(t,h)) + geom_line(linewidth=.7,color="#245C89") +
  geom_vline(xintercept=c(4,21,52,76),linetype=3,color="grey60") +
  annotate("text",x=c(4,21,52,76),y=c(3,37,34,3),label=c("ATOT","TOC","TOD","ALDT"),size=2.4) +
  annotate("text",x=c(12,36,64),y=41,label=c("Climb","Enroute","Descent"),size=2.7) +
  labs(x="Elapsed time (schematic)",y="Altitude (schematic)") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0,44)) + theme_classic(base_size=8) + theme(axis.text=element_blank(),axis.ticks=element_blank())
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
paper_table(data.frame(
  Family=c("Operational", "LTO / runway", "Airport-distance", "Pressure altitude", "Level intervals"),
  Milestones=c("AOBT, ATOT, TOC, TOD, ALDT, AIBT", "ERWY, DLTO, ALTO, XRWY", "D040/D100/D200; A200/A100/A040", "D_FL075/100/180; A_FL180/100/075", "LVL_START, LVL_END; segment ID")),
  "Milestone families retained in the study model.",c(.25,.69))
```

Airport-distance anchors refer to great-circle radii around airport coordinates. **Aerodrome GCD** is the endpoint-to-endpoint distance used for stage-length stratification; cumulative flown distance is a separate quantity. Pressure-altitude crossings retain direction and differ from height above local terrain. Airport coordinates supply sourced proxies for ARP.

TOC marks entry to the initial sustained enroute level and TOD marks exit from the final sustained enroute level. The interval between them can contain step climbs and descents. In a boundary-definition sensitivity, the initial departure and final arrival 200 NM windows establish the relevant near-ceiling altitude: within 1,000 ft or 3% of the window maximum, whichever is greater. Select the first complete qualifying level for TOC and the last for TOD; the circle-crossing timestamp does not replace a level boundary. Where a circle does not discriminate, use the airborne-profile ceiling. Compare this **level-envelope** definition with the source-selected TOC/TOD using the same flights.

## Study data and analysis cohorts

The summer-2025 study uses fourteen QAR-derived Chinese batches and a European sample combining G2G milestones with M3 trajectory support. Chinese fuel quantities derive from recorded engine flow; European quantities are model-based [@eurocontrolAEM]. Profile characterisation uses time and pressure altitude independently of fuel magnitude.

```{r}
#| results: asis
d <- data.frame(
  Item=c("Source flights", "Analysis flights", "Common-support flights", "Airports / directed pairs", "Aircraft types (source)", "GCD range (NM, source)", "GCD median (NM, source)"),
  China=c(fmt(inv("CHN","INPUT")),fmt(inv("CHN","RETAINED")),fmt(inv("CHN","COMMON_SUPPORT")),paste(inv("CHN","AIRPORTS"),inv("CHN","ROUTES"),sep=" / "),inv("CHN","TYPES"),paste(fmt(inv("CHN","GCD_MIN")),fmt(inv("CHN","GCD_MAX")),sep="--"),fmt(inv("CHN","GCD_P50"))),
  Europe=c(fmt(inv("EUR","INPUT")),fmt(inv("EUR","RETAINED")),fmt(inv("EUR","COMMON_SUPPORT")),paste(inv("EUR","AIRPORTS"),inv("EUR","ROUTES"),sep=" / "),inv("EUR","TYPES"),paste(fmt(inv("EUR","GCD_MIN")),fmt(inv("EUR","GCD_MAX")),sep="--"),fmt(inv("EUR","GCD_P50"))))
paper_table(d,"Study sample and aircraft/distance support.",c(.46,.24,.24))
```

The Chinese sample covers ZSSS connections with ZBAA, ZLXY and ZPPP in both directions. The European source sample covers 11 airports and 22 directed pairs. Counts and endpoint-distance summaries describe the source sample; subsequent comparisons use the eligible analysis flights.

```{r}
#| results: asis
t <- analysis$types |> filter(INPUT_CHN>0)
paper_table(data.frame(Type=t$TYPE, `CHN input / kept`=paste(t$INPUT_CHN,t$RETAINED_CHN,sep=" / "),
 `EUR input / kept`=paste(t$INPUT_EUR,t$RETAINED_EUR,sep=" / "),check.names=FALSE),
 "Aircraft types occurring in China, with European support. Additional EUR-only types enter the overview.",c(.22,.34,.38))
```

Exact aircraft variants remain separate. Aircraft without two-region support contribute to regional characterisation rather than paired comparisons. Engine variants are not distinguished in the present grouping. Eligibility requires distinct, ordered airborne phase boundaries and plausible time, altitude and position support. Flights are selected for the metric being compared; the per-cell counts specify the comparison denominator.

## Descriptors and comparison design

Report flight-weighted P20/P50/P80 of GCD, airborne duration, phase durations, enroute share, and TOC/TOD altitude. For comparison, use exact aircraft type × shared 100 NM GCD bands with at least 30 independent flights **in each region**. This is a support rule rather than a power calculation. Regional overviews describe composition; cell-specific results compare like aircraft and stage length.

Estimate altitude residence from the altitude-time profile, retaining Chinese milestone and paired level-boundary knots and European M3 trajectory knots. Interpolate altitude linearly between successive timestamps and split intervals at each pressure-altitude-band crossing. This is a trajectory-reconstruction assumption, rather than a claim of continuous observation. A resolution sensitivity retains only spans bracketed within 300 s. Source sampling and smoothing remain properties of the measurement design.

Clip each reconstructed trajectory interval to TOC--TOD and integrate residence time within common pressure-altitude bands without double-counting. For flight $i$ and band $b$, report minutes $L_{ib}$ and share $L_{ib}/T_i$, where $T_i$ is the whole TOC--TOD duration. Altitude-changing intervals contribute time to each band crossed. Time lacking a bracketing altitude pair remains **unbracketed**, with no extrapolation. These metrics measure altitude exposure rather than level-off or interruption counts.

Two summaries answer different questions: the mean across flights of band minutes/shares describes operational exposure; the distribution of each flight's time-weighted enroute altitude describes the levels occupied. Neither is a count of trajectory points. For the boundary sensitivity, sustained levels last at least 120 s, have absolute vertical rate no greater than 300 ft/min and span no more than 1,000 ft. The level-envelope rule uses complete qualified levels and does not bridge M3 gaps beyond 300 s. The comparison retains identical flights under both definitions and reports support counts.

## Lookup-table construction

- Key: **source/region × aircraft type/engine group × GCD band × phase × common profile class**. Aircraft variants remain distinct; the engine dimension is explicitly *not stratified* where engine identity is not supplied.
- Marginal baseline rows pool all profiles within an aircraft/distance/phase cell. They are not a profile class and are kept separate from conditional rows. The first conditional enroute classes use each flight's time-weighted mean pressure altitude: below FL300, FL300--339, or FL340 and above. These fixed thresholds have the same meaning in both regions.
- For source-window endpoints, compute fuel $F=F_{cum}(t_1)-F_{cum}(t_0)$, duration $T$, and flown distance $D$. Summarise independent-flight distributions of $F$, $T$, $F/T$ and $F/D$ with P20/P50/P80. GCD defines the stage band and is not the denominator of a phase's kg/NM rate.
- Publish metric-specific $n$; fuel/time and fuel/distance eligibility can differ. Suppress percentiles below 30 observations and distinguish empty cells from classes not assigned. A paired comparison additionally requires support in both regions.
- Retain the source fuel convention and phase-boundary definition with every cell. Percentiles of individual rates are calculated directly; a ratio of percentile fuel to percentile duration is a different statistic. A row's separate percentile columns do not describe one joint reference flight.

# Results and discussion

## Stage length and profile composition

```{r}
#| label: fig-stage
#| fig-cap: "GCD distributions in the screened samples. The different route mixtures motivate distance stratification."
#| fig-width: 3.45
#| fig-height: 1.85
plots$stage
```

Screened sample median GCD is `r fmt(med("CHN","GCD_NM"))` NM in China and `r fmt(med("EUR","GCD_NM"))` NM in Europe. Chinese source routes occupy only three endpoint distances; Europe includes much shorter stages. The longest Chinese stages have no European distance counterpart in this extraction. Overall regional phase differences therefore combine route, aircraft and profile composition.

```{r}
#| results: asis
labels <- c(GCD_NM="GCD (NM)", AIRBORNE_MIN="Airborne (min)", CLIMB_MIN="Climb (min)", ENROUTE_MIN="Enroute (min)", DESCENT_MIN="Descent (min)", ENROUTE_SHARE="Enroute share (%)", ALT_FT_TOC="TOC altitude (100 ft)", ALT_FT_TOD="TOD altitude (100 ft)")
metrics <- names(labels)
sc <- c(1,1,1,1,1,100,.01,.01)
paper_table(data.frame(Metric=unname(labels), China=mapply(function(m,s)cell("CHN",m,s),metrics,sc), Europe=mapply(function(m,s)cell("EUR",m,s),metrics,sc)),
 "Screened sample descriptors: P50 [P20; P80]. Unadjusted regional summaries.",c(.34,.30,.30))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-timing
#| fig-cap: "Phase duration distributions for ATOT--TOC--TOD--ALDT. Panels have different horizontal scales."
#| fig-width: 3.45
#| fig-height: 1.9
plots$timing
```

Median TOC--TOD duration is `r fmt(med("CHN","ENROUTE_MIN"),1)` min in China and `r fmt(med("EUR","ENROUTE_MIN"),1)` min in Europe, with median airborne shares of `r fmt(100*med("CHN","ENROUTE_SHARE"),1)`% and `r fmt(100*med("EUR","ENROUTE_SHARE"),1)`%. Missing or coincident boundaries are excluded rather than interpreted as unusually short enroute operation; genuinely zero-cruise profiles require separate identification.

## Comparable aircraft and distance support

```{r}
#| results: asis
s <- analysis$support |> filter(COMMON)
paper_table(data.frame(Type=s$TYPE,`GCD band (NM)`=paste(s$BAND100,s$BAND100+99,sep="--"),China=s$CHN,Europe=s$EUR,check.names=FALSE),
 "Common-support cells; independent screened flight counts.",c(.18,.34,.20,.22))
```

Six cells support comparisons: five exact aircraft types over 600--699 NM, plus A21N over 500--599 NM. These contain `r fmt(inv("CHN","COMMON_SUPPORT"))` Chinese and `r fmt(inv("EUR","COMMON_SUPPORT"))` European flights. Widebodies lack the required joint support despite substantial Chinese source counts. Equal type and distance band do not equalise engines, operators, payload, winds, direction or airport procedures.

```{r}
#| results: asis
dd <- analysis$differences |> filter(METRIC %in% c("CLIMB_MIN","ENROUTE_MIN","DESCENT_MIN")) |>
  select(TYPE,BAND100,METRIC,CHN_MINUS_EUR) |> pivot_wider(names_from=METRIC,values_from=CHN_MINUS_EUR)
paper_table(data.frame(Cell=paste(dd$TYPE,dd$BAND100),Climb=fmt(dd$CLIMB_MIN,1),Enroute=fmt(dd$ENROUTE_MIN,1),Descent=fmt(dd$DESCENT_MIN,1)),
 "Median-duration differences (China minus Europe, min); cell label gives type and band lower bound.",c(.31,.21,.21,.21))
```

Chinese median climb duration exceeds the European median by approximately 2.6--8.6 min across these cells. Enroute median differences are much smaller, approximately -5.2 to +1.9 min. Descent differences vary in sign. The aggregate impression of a longer Chinese enroute phase should therefore not carry directly into fuel-burn interpretation. These are descriptive within-cell comparisons rather than estimates of an ATM effect.

## Time spent at enroute levels

```{r}
#| label: fig-enroute-exposure
#| fig-cap: "Mean flight share of source-defined TOC--TOD time by reconstructed pressure-altitude band. Grey denotes unbracketed time. Each row sums to 100%; altitude exposure is distinct from smoothness."
#| fig-width: 3.45
#| fig-height: 3.15
plot_enroute_exposure(enroute)
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
band_minutes <- enroute$band_summary |> filter(WINDOW=="Source") |>
  mutate(METRIC=case_when(BAND%in%c("<FL240","FL240-299")~"Below FL300",
    BAND%in%c("FL340-379",">=FL380")~"At/above FL340",TRUE~"Other")) |>
  group_by(REGION,TYPE,BAND100,METRIC) |> summarise(MIN=sum(MEAN_MIN),.groups="drop") |>
  filter(METRIC!="Other") |> pivot_wider(names_from=REGION,values_from=MIN) |>
  mutate(VALUE=paste(fmt(CHN,1),fmt(EUR,1),sep=" / ")) |>
  select(TYPE,BAND100,METRIC,VALUE) |> pivot_wider(names_from=METRIC,values_from=VALUE)
paper_table(data.frame(Cell=paste(band_minutes$TYPE,band_minutes$BAND100),
  `Below FL300`=band_minutes$`Below FL300`,`At/above FL340`=band_minutes$`At/above FL340`,check.names=FALSE),
  "Mean minutes per flight by altitude range, China / Europe. Source-defined TOC--TOD; cell label gives type and GCD-band lower bound.",c(.30,.32,.32))
```

The altitude-band view distinguishes the levels occupied from the overall duration of the enroute phase. The comparison retains both absolute minutes and shares: a larger share at a given level can coexist with fewer minutes when the enroute interval is shorter. Unbracketed time is reported explicitly rather than redistributed over observed altitude bands.

```{r}
#| results: asis
level_alt <- enroute$paired_summary |> select(REGION,TYPE,BAND100,WINDOW,MEAN_ALT_P50) |>
  mutate(VALUE=fmt(MEAN_ALT_P50/100,0)) |> select(-MEAN_ALT_P50) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from=c(REGION,WINDOW),values_from=VALUE)
paper_table(data.frame(Cell=paste(level_alt$TYPE,level_alt$BAND100),
  China=paste(level_alt$CHN_Source,level_alt$`CHN_Level envelope`,sep=" / "),
  Europe=paste(level_alt$EUR_Source,level_alt$`EUR_Level envelope`,sep=" / ")),
  "Median flight time-weighted enroute altitude (100 ft): source / level-envelope windows. Identical flights under both definitions.",c(.34,.30,.30))
```

```{r}
#| include: false
level_diffs <- enroute$paired_summary |> select(REGION,TYPE,BAND100,WINDOW,MEAN_ALT_P50) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from=REGION,values_from=MEAN_ALT_P50) |> mutate(DIFF=CHN-EUR)
source_diffs <- filter(level_diffs,WINDOW=="Source")$DIFF
alt_diffs <- filter(level_diffs,WINDOW=="Level envelope")$DIFF
```

Chinese median time-weighted enroute altitude is lower within every shared cell: by `r fmt(min(abs(source_diffs)),0)`--`r fmt(max(abs(source_diffs)),0)` ft using source boundaries. Under the level-envelope definition the range is `r fmt(min(abs(alt_diffs)),0)`--`r fmt(max(abs(alt_diffs)),0)` ft. Thus the altitude contrast concerns residence within the enroute interval as well as the TOC/TOD endpoints. Its magnitude varies with aircraft/stage length and with the chosen phase boundary; it does not itself establish a fuel penalty or an ATM cause.

## Sensitivity to TOC/TOD definition

```{r}
#| results: asis
bs <- enroute$boundary_summary |> group_by(REGION) |>
  summarise(Paired=sum(PAIRED_N),TOC=100*sum(TOC_WITHIN_60S)/sum(PAIRED_N),
    TOD=100*sum(TOD_WITHIN_60S)/sum(PAIRED_N),.groups="drop")
paper_table(data.frame(Region=bs$REGION,Flights=fmt(bs$Paired),
  `TOC (%)`=fmt(bs$TOC,1),`TOD (%)`=fmt(bs$TOD,1),check.names=FALSE),
  "Agreement of source and level-envelope boundaries within 60 s, on flights supporting both definitions.",c(.23,.23,.24,.24))
```

This sensitivity separates a change in operational description from a change in definition. A level-envelope interval can retain an initial capped level or a final step descent that a single-cruise interpretation assigns to climb or descent. Both rules therefore accompany the altitude result; comparisons of enroute duration use the same paired cohort rather than differences between separately selected samples.

```{r}
#| results: asis
paired_time <- enroute$paired_summary |> select(REGION,TYPE,BAND100,WINDOW,ENROUTE_P50) |>
  mutate(VALUE=fmt(ENROUTE_P50,1)) |> select(-ENROUTE_P50) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from=c(REGION,WINDOW),values_from=VALUE)
paper_table(data.frame(Cell=paste(paired_time$TYPE,paired_time$BAND100),
  China=paste(paired_time$CHN_Source,paired_time$`CHN_Level envelope`,sep=" / "),
  Europe=paste(paired_time$EUR_Source,paired_time$`EUR_Level envelope`,sep=" / ")),
  "Median enroute duration (min), source / level-envelope windows, on the paired cohort.",c(.34,.30,.30))
```

## Partially populated lookup grid

The marginal layer spans the six aircraft/GCD cells and all three airborne phases. The conditional layer retains enroute altitude classes; climb/descent interruption classes occupy separate reserved slots. Source-region and the unstratified engine dimension remain explicit.

```{r}
#| results: asis
coverage <- lookup$profile_support |> filter(PROFILE_CLASS!="Altitude unobserved") |>
  mutate(ENTRY=paste0(CHN," / ",EUR,if_else(PAIRED_SUPPORT," *",""))) |>
  select(TYPE,BAND100,PROFILE_CLASS,ENTRY) |> pivot_wider(names_from=PROFILE_CLASS,values_from=ENTRY)
paper_table(data.frame(Cell=paste(coverage$TYPE,coverage$BAND100),
  `<FL300`=coverage$`Below FL300`,`FL300-339`=coverage$`FL300-339`,`FL340+`=coverage$`FL340+`,check.names=FALSE),
  "Enroute lookup support: eligible fuel observations, China / Europe. * marks at least 30 in both regions; engine variants are not stratified.",c(.25,.23,.23,.23))
```

```{r}
#| include: false
paired_fuel_cells <- lookup$profile_support |> filter(PAIRED_SUPPORT)
```

`r nrow(paired_fuel_cells)` profile-conditioned enroute cells meet the fuel-support rule in both regions. Cells with lower support retain their counts without published percentiles. Missing climb/descent classifications remain unassigned rather than becoming continuous profiles or zero-fuel entries.

```{r}
#| results: asis
example <- lookup$grid |> filter(TYPE=="A21N",BAND100==500,PHASE=="Enroute",PROFILE_CLASS=="FL340+",
  METRIC%in%c("FUEL_KG","DURATION_MIN","KG_MIN","KG_NM")) |>
  mutate(DIGITS=case_when(METRIC=="FUEL_KG"~0,METRIC=="KG_NM"~2,TRUE~1),
    VALUE=if_else(STATUS=="Populated",paste0(mapply(fmt,P20,DIGITS),"/",mapply(fmt,P50,DIGITS),"/",mapply(fmt,P80,DIGITS)),"--")) |>
  select(REGION,METRIC,N,VALUE) |> pivot_wider(names_from=REGION,values_from=c(N,VALUE)) |>
  mutate(METRIC=factor(METRIC,levels=c("FUEL_KG","DURATION_MIN","KG_MIN","KG_NM"),
    labels=c("Fuel (kg)","Time (min)","kg/min","kg/NM"))) |> arrange(METRIC)
paper_table(data.frame(Metric=example$METRIC,China=example$VALUE_CHN,Europe=example$VALUE_EUR,
  `n CHN/EUR`=paste(example$N_CHN,example$N_EUR,sep=" / "),check.names=FALSE),
  "Example conditional lookup: A21N, 500--599 NM, enroute, mean altitude at/above FL340; P20 / P50 / P80. Engines not stratified.",c(.22,.25,.25,.22))
```

The example illustrates reference distributions rather than a regional efficiency ranking. Aircraft type, GCD band and altitude class do not equalise payload, wind, speed, operator or fuel-source methodology. The marginal profile distribution remains a separate regional result; conditional cells cannot describe how frequently each profile occurs.

## Profile context and conditional consumption

- Climb/descent profile characterisation: paired level segments, phase-clipped union time and altitude distinguish interruptions from normal sustained enroute flight. Accepted CCO/CDO intervals supply the European terminal-phase evidence.
- Profile classes: total level time/share, interruption count, longest interruption and altitude are separate climb/descent descriptors. Common class thresholds apply in both regions; unknown coverage remains distinct from genuinely uninterrupted flight.
- Retain the **regional profile distribution** when adding conditional consumption. Matching on profile alone could conceal a difference in how often interrupted profiles occur.
- Conditional-consumption lookup: **aircraft/engine group × GCD band × phase × common profile class**, retaining source/region, with fuel kg, duration, kg/min, kg/NM, P20/P50/P80 and independent-flight support. Total fuel remains alongside rates; lower kg/min need not imply lower phase fuel.
- Percentiles are descriptive references. P20 is not an attainable optimum; P50--P20 is not an ATM-recoverable saving. Fuel comparisons must also distinguish recorded and modelled fuel and retain the European original/adjusted fuel convention.

# Conclusion

- Summarise within-cell differences in enroute duration and time at sustained levels, with the TOC/TOD sensitivity.
- State the reach of the selected routes/operators; distinguish regional profile composition from conditional consumption.
- Separate descriptive fuel references from achievable savings or regional-efficiency claims.
